newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS sees good traffic in Q1 '97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: SAS sees good traffic in Q1 '97 - paper.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS said traffic volumes in the first quarter of 1997 had been decent, a Swedish business daily reported on Friday.
SAS chief executive Jan Stenberg told Dagens Industri that the airline's effort to trim costs and boost productivity had made an impact in the first three months.
"In terms of traffic volumes SAS had a decent first quarter," Stenberg told the newspaper.
SAS will report its earnings for the first quarter on May 6.
Stenberg said the 1996 result was a disappointment which prompted the drive to boost productivity.
Last year the airline, that is owned by the governments of Sweden, Norway and Denmark and private investors, posted a pre-tax profit of 1.82 billion crowns against 2.63 billion crowns in 1995.
It blamed increased competition for the 31 percent fall.
"I think you can already see the result of our efforts to increase productivity and become more cost effective," Stenberg said.
He said there was still room to cut costs further and increase income.
